issues.title: Interceptors response config.data returns stringified object
issues.body:
<!-- Click "Preview" for a more readable version --

instance.interceptors.response's config.data returns stringified object

- Read all our documentation, especially the [README](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/master/README.md). It may contain information that helps you solve your issue.
- Ensure your issue isn't already [reported](https://github.com/axios/axios/issues?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Aissue).
- If you aren't sure that the issue is caused by Axios or you just need help, please use [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/axios) or [our chat](https://gitter.im/mzabriskie/axios).
- If you're reporting a bug, ensure it isn't already fixed in the latest Axios version.
- Don't remove any title of the issue template, or it will be treated as invalid by the bot.

⚠️👆 Feel free to these instructions before submitting the issue 👆⚠️
-->

#### Describe the bug
The config.data set to the object type in the interceptor request  but in interceptor.response it returns stringified object

[#3986](https://github.com/axios/axios/issues/3986#issue-981106758) I think it's the same  issue.

#### To Reproduce
Code snippet to reproduce, ideally that will work by pasting into something like https://npm.runkit.com/axios, a hosted solution, or a repository that illustrates the issue. **If your problem is not reproducible, please file under Support or Usage Question**

```js
var axios = require("axios")

const defaultConfig = {
    baseURL: '',
    timeout: 120 * 1000,
    withCredentials: true,
    headers: {
      'content-type': 'application/json',
      'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*',
    },
  };

const request = ({ method, url, data, config, specificInterceptor }) => {
    const finalConfig = { ...defaultConfig, ...config };
    const instance = axios.create(finalConfig);
  
    instance.interceptors.request.use(config => {
      const timeData = { startTime: new Date(), endTime: undefined };
      config.data = timeData;
      return config;
    });
  
    //response interceptor
    instance.interceptors.response.use(
      (response) => {
        console.log(typeof response.config.data, response.config.data)
        if (response.status === 200) {
          return response.data;
        } else {
          return Promise.reject(new Error('this error was thrown by api', response.data));
        }
      },
      (error) => Promise.reject(error),
    );
  
    if (data) {
      Object.keys(data).forEach(item => {
        if (item && (data[item] === undefined || data[item] === null)) {
          delete data[item];
        }
      });
    }
  
    return instance({
      method: method || 'get',
      url,
      data: method === 'post' && data,
    });
  };

  request({ url: `https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/todos/1` });
```

#### Expected behavior
A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen.

#### Environment
 - Axios Version [^0.27.2]
 - Browser [Chrome]
 - Node.js Version [17.7.2]
 - Additional Library Versions [e.g. React 18.2]

#### Additional context/Screenshots
Add any other context about the problem here. If applicable, add screenshots to help explain.

comments.body:
Thanks for the report. Browser `Network Error` stack traces generally point to the adapter/error construction site because the browser does not expose a deeper cause for many network failures. This is the same platform limitation discussed in other network-error issues.

I am closing this as answered. For production debugging, capture request metadata in your own wrapper/interceptor and check browser console/network diagnostics for CORS, mixed-content, and connectivity failures.

issues.title: Authorization header on Instance vs Request
issues.body:
### Describe the issue

I understand that on a request's configuration the `auth` will take precedence over a custom `Authorization` header as fixed in #397. But when it comes to configuring an instance I thought that a request would override it.

How come this is not supported? Is it undesirable?

### Example Code

```js
const instance = Axios.create({ url: 'http://localhost:8080', auth: { username: '', password: '' } })

await instance.get('/path', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer abc123' } })
```


### Expected behavior

The url `http://localhost:8080/path` to be called with the header `Bearer abd123` rather than `Basic usrpsw`.

comments.author: ismaeeelxd

comments.body:
That sort of defeats the purpose of an "instance". I would rather configure an instance to have Basic Auth and override it when JWT's are relevant.
Sure I could encode the basic auth credentials myself directly into the Authorization header but that defeats the purpose of `auth`.

On the other hand if I avoid using the instance to pre-configure the basic auth in `auth` then every separate request from that instance needs to inject it, which is just a nuisance but entirely avoidable.
comments.author: karloluis

comments.body:
To address your comment directly. A bit nuanced but hopefully it helps shed light on what I think caused issues for me.

The docs state this auth vs header without distinction between options in a request and those based on a pre-configured instance. Since the instance obfuscates the use of `auth` it is reasonable to assume that it would cause confusion. 
> ie. "I did not state `auth` in the `.post('/', opts)` options, but rather a JWT. Why am I seeing something else?" Which is caused by the instance declared potentially somewhere else.

issues.title: A problem with setting AxiosError.prototype.toJSON
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`util.inherits` fails on `Object.assign(props)` when `Error.prototype.toJSON`  is already defined as a non-writable. 

We're using a library that adds a toJSON to the prototype of Error.
It does it using something in the spirit of:
```
Object.defineProperty(Error.prorotype, 'toJSON', { configurable: true, writable: false, enumerable: false, value() {
  /* some customization code  that makes sure name, stack and any own property passes */ 
})
```
Then, `axios/lib/util.js:inerit` fails on `Object.assign`.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4147783-fe1c-4ed4-a2eb-bd4919cae0a8)

Also - see reproduction below.


### To Reproduce

Case isolated in the code snippet below.

### Code snippet

```js
Object.defineProperty(Error.prototype, 'toJSON', {
  configurable: true,
  writable: false,
  enumerable: false,
  value: function foo() { return {} }
})

const utils = (await import(path.join(process.cwd(), 'node_modules/axios/lib/utils.js'))).default

function MyError() { }

//This does not work (throws):
utils.inherits(MyError, Error, { toJSON() { return {} } }) //<-- throws: TypeError: Cannot assign to read only property 'toJSON' of object 'Error'

//This does not throw, and works as expected:
const util = require('node:util')
util.inherits(MyError, Error, { toJSON() { return {} } })
```


### Expected behavior

- Should not throw
- Should set the toJSON on the extended prototype

### Axios Version

1.7.7

### Adapter Version

_No response_

### Browser

_No response_

### Browser Version

_No response_

### Node.js Version

v20.18.0

### OS

Fedora in WSL.
Reproduced on my Win 11 also with node 20.12.2

### Additional Library Versions

_No response_

### Additional context/Screenshots

_No response_
issues.author: osher

comments.body:
This issue does not seem to be a bug; rather, it is expected behavior.

For property inheritance, Axios's `utils.inherits()` assigns properties to the child's `constructor.prototype` using the `Object.assign()` method.

Because `Object.assign()` *assigns* properties, it could throw a TypeError if a property is non-writable, as explained in the [MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/assign#description). According to your code snippet, you defined `toJSON` as non-writable property, so it's natural for it to throw.

However, Node's `util.inherits()` does not provide functionality that inherits properties by assigning them. It only accepts two parameters: the child and the super constructor.

So on your working example `util.inherits(MyError, Error, { toJSON() { return {} } })`, the third parameter will just be ignored because functions in JavaScript do not throw errors for extra arguments.

Here's the actual code definition in node: [util.js:321](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v20.18.0/lib/util.js#L321)

And here's the code in axios: [utils.js:360](https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/main/lib/utils.js#L360)
